title: Testing and improving a stop smoking app for pregnancy
official: Feasibility and optimisation of the Smoke Free app for pregnancy (eSupport)
summary:
Background and study aims 
This study aims to test and improve a pregnancy-specific version of the Smoke Free app. This version is designed to offer support similar to NHS care for stopping smoking during pregnancy, but it can be accessed at any time without needing to speak to a human advisor. Instead, it includes a friendly chatbot that delivers advice on how to quit smoking, an information library and supportive notifications and messages. The chatbot can also help participants choose suitable quit products, such as nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) or a vape (e-cigarette), if needed - but a human advisor will check this and verify eligibility (aged 18+ years for vapes). The app has been designed with people who have smoked during pregnancy and health professionals.

Who can participate? 
Adult participants who currently smoke, are aged 18 years or older, are less than 25 weeks pregnant and are willing to make a quit attempt.

What does the study involve? 
Participants will be recruited in 3-4 groups, one after another, to test the app, or parts of it. After consent and baseline data collection, participants will be asked to download the app, answer questions about themselves and their smoking, set a quit date, used the app for up to 6 weeks and provide feedback on their experiences in an end-of-study survey/interview). Feedback will be used to make changes to the app after each group, to be tested in the next.
For those who wish to use NRT or a vape to support a quit attempt, these will be provided for up to 4 weeks. This allows time for participants to start using the app and for products to be deliver. Participants will be offered a referral to local stop smoking services if they would like further support.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Participants will receive usual NHS care for smoking cessation in pregnancy, comprising behavioural support and offer of NRT (and/or vape) to aid their quit attempt. Prior to this, as part of the study, they will also receive free NRT or vape alongside the digital stop smoking intervention. 
The main objective of this study is to help test and optimise the new digital stop smoking intervention, which might be gratifying to people taking part.
The study is considered to be of low risk to participants. 
1. There is a potential low risk due to vapes being available as part of the study intervention. 
In England, vapes are often used by stop-smoking services to support smoking cessation in pregnancy. Some maternity services have commissioned vape provision in pregnancy independently; this has been further supported by the government’s ‘Swap to Stop’ scheme, providing free vape starter kits to encourage people to stop smoking, and has approximately 93% of local authorities participating. 
The use of vapes for smoking cessation in pregnancy is supported by the Smoking in Pregnancy Challenge Group, which recognises that while NRT remains the recommended and preferred option, vapes should be considered as a safer alternative to smoking.
2. Participants will have the option to self-enrol in the study, without speaking to a researcher during the consent process. This poses some risk of participants not giving a truly informed consent. To minimise this, we offer the option to speak to the researcher at each stage of the enrolment process and participants will also be offered access to PIS, summary PIS and additional information, such as FAQ page. 
This is in line with how engagement with the app will be initiated in real life – people will use links/QR codes to find out more about the support and sign up at a time that is convenient to them. This will allow engagement outside of office hours and without delay. 
IP addresses will be checked to avoid multiple enrolment from the same participant; GP and hospital contact details will be collected and used to establish the person’s identity. 
3. Potential burdens – participants will be asked to complete an end of study survey and may be asked to take part in an interview over a video or telephone call. This will take no longer than 90 minutes total (30 survey and 60 interview). The participants will not be expected to travel to appointments, all data collection will be done online or over the telephone. They will be compensated for their time with gift cards (total £30). 
Participants will require some time to install, sign up to and use the study app. The app is free of cost to the participants.

Where is the study run from?  
University of East Anglia (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
September 2026 to August 2027

Who is funding the study? 
The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Prof. Felix Naughton, f.naughton@uea.ac.uk

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Currently pregnant (less than 25 weeks), and has been referred for (or received or attended) an appointment as part of standard antenatal care
2. Aged 18 years or over (there is no upper age limit)
3. Currently smoking at least one tobacco cigarette every day
4. Interested in receiving app-based help to stop smoking, which includes behavioural support (e.g. quit tips), the offer of free nicotine replacement therapy or a vape (if wanted), and being willing to set a quit date within 14 days of app enrolment
5. Owns and uses an Android or Apple smartphone, is willing to install the study’s stop smoking app, and can send and receive SMS text messages
6. Agrees to give feedback on their experiences with the app at the end of the study, by questionnaire (online or paper) and optional interview (video call or telephone)
7. Able to understand written and spoken English
Exclusion criteria:
1. Currently receiving formal stop smoking support that includes free NRT or a vape (e.g. from an NHS midwife/GP/pharmacist, or from a stop smoking service, or from an app)
2. Currently taking part in another stop smoking study
3. Only vaping (not smoking tobacco cigarettes)
4. Smoking tobacco cigarettes less than daily
